clue.text: Where to find transport for a fish? On a boat?

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece set on another simply follows it

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish
an ark is a boat, as Noah's was

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about how a fish might be carried, perhaps aboard a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A parking area is where cars, the commonest personal transport, are left and found again.

clue.text: Run bath and put something naughty in drink

indicators.note: in says the naughty thing is placed inside the rearranged letters
to run here is to go wrong or loose, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone runs a bath and slips a little mischief into a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' is the anagram signal, not a running bath, and 'put ... in' is split around the sin it inserts; the drink is the green spirit famed in Belle Epoque Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong green aniseed-flavoured spirit, once banned in France, is a drink.

clue.text: Design end product using machines

parts.note: to design a thing is to plan it

indicators.note: end of the word product points to its final letter

explanation.surface: An instruction to design the final output of an automated factory process.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Design' looks like the definition; it is the verb giving PLAN, and the definition is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Industrial machinery is collectively called plant, as in heavy plant on a building site.

clue.text: Criticism for salesman out on the tiles?

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
read literally, being out on the tiles puts you up on the roof

explanation.surface: Disapproval of a travelling salesman who spends his nights partying.
explanation.walkthrough: Out on the tiles is British slang for a night of revelry; taken literally, tiles are on a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A reproof is a rebuke or a word of criticism.

clue.text: Evidence of virus disputed in report

indicators.note: in report means the phrase is heard spoken rather than spelled

parts.note: a matter that is disputed is at issue

explanation.surface: Proof of an infection is contested in some official document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report' looks like a written document; here it signals speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The sound of a sneeze is a sign someone has caught a cold virus.

clue.text: Top trio takes composer on tour

indicators.note: top of the word trio in a down clue is its first letter

parts.note: Maurice Ravel was the French composer of Bolero

explanation.surface: A leading trio of musicians takes a composer's works on tour.
explanation.definitionFit: To tour is to travel from place to place, and a tour is a journey.

clue.text: Composed crude song and fished for freebies

indicators.note: composed means put together, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A musician wrote a vulgar ditty and angled for free stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrounge is to cadge things for nothing; fished for means tried to get.

clue.text: Filthy location for outside broadcast

parts.note: a scene is a location where something happens

explanation.surface: A dirty, grimy site chosen for a television outside broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene means indecent or disgusting, the moral sense of filthy.

clue.text: They observe transport site movements

indicators.note: movements suggests the letters moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: Enthusiasts watch the comings and goings at a railway or bus depot.
explanation.walkthrough: Trainspotters are hobbyists who log the numbers of passing locomotives.
explanation.definitionFit: Trainspotters watch and record trains, so they are observers by hobby.

clue.text: Where most live overseas, I aim to hide away

indicators.note: to hide away says the answer lies concealed inside the following words

explanation.surface: An expatriate's plan to vanish and live abroad somewhere far away.
explanation.definitionFit: Most of the world's population lives on the continent of Asia.

clue.text: Ground too hard for farmers to turn over after first ploughing

indicators.note: after says the rearranged letters follow the opening letter
first of the word ploughing means its opening letter
to turn over soil is to churn it, so these letters are churned

explanation.surface: Farmland frozen so solid that farmers cannot turn it over once ploughing begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Permanently frozen subsoil is ground too hard to dig.

clue.text: Owen to run around with quick-fire passing

indicators.note: to run around is to move about, so these letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: A footballer called Owen runs around exchanging quick passes.
explanation.walkthrough: Owen evokes the footballer Michael Owen, fitting the passing play.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-two in football is a quick give-and-go pass between two players.

clue.text: Water coolers (summer treats) eat up power

indicators.note: eat up says the treats swallow the next piece inside them

parts.note: ices are frozen treats eaten in summer
in maths the cube is a power, the third

explanation.surface: Ice lollies are devoured by an electrical supply, said of drinks chillers.
explanation.definitionFit: Small blocks of frozen water are dropped into drinks to cool them.

clue.text: Cod etc show desire for conflict, says Spooner

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words

explanation.surface: Someone eager for a fight puts on a show of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of FIGHT WISH gives WIGHT FISH, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cod, haddock and similar pale-fleshed sea fish are classed as white fish.

clue.text: Where tramlines turn around

indicators.note: turn around asks the letters to be reversed and mixed into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Asking where tram routes loop back at the end of the line.
explanation.definitionFit: Termini are the end stations where trams turn back.

clue.text: Correspond about being overwhelmed by time

indicators.note: being overwhelmed by means engulfed, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: an age is a period of time
re is Latin-derived for about, regarding

explanation.surface: Letters exchanged on a subject get swamped as the hours pass.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that correspond match or concur.

clue.text: Give relief to one that's redundant

definitions.meaning: to let them off something unpleasant
an extra kept in reserve is surplus and not needed

explanation.surface: Being kind to someone who has just lost their job.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare means both to let off and something surplus to need.

clue.text: One of the nouveau riche from Peru in van crash

indicators.note: a crash smashes things, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A newly rich person is caught in a van accident in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart newly risen to wealth is a parvenu, a French word for one who has arrived.

clue.text: Giant peach grower had a droll invention

indicators.note: an invention is something made up, so these letters are reconfigured

explanation.surface: A horticulturalist growing enormous fruit had a comical gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: The author wrote James and the Giant Peach, so he grew a giant peach in fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: The children's author made the giant peach grow in his story.

clue.text: Feel poorly — setback for Boatman and his French affair

indicators.note: setback says the word for feeling poorly runs backwards

parts.note: to ail is to feel poorly
the setter, Boatman, refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: An ill setter confesses to a French love affair.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a secret romantic or sexual relationship.

clue.text: Fish consumed on pier

parts.note: having eaten something, you had it
a dock is a pier or wharf for ships

explanation.surface: A fish eaten on a seaside jetty.
explanation.definitionFit: Haddock is a North Atlantic food fish related to cod.

clue.text: Worse for wear after opening bottle and gaming

indicators.note: opening of the word bottle is its first letter

parts.note: lotto is a game of chance, gaming

explanation.surface: Someone the worse for wear after cracking a bottle and gambling.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is slang for very drunk, the worse for wear from drink.

clue.text: Child allowed a tiny peach, perhaps

parts.note: fruit can mean offspring, as in the fruit of the womb

explanation.surface: A child is permitted a small peach to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruitlet is a small fruit; a tiny peach is an example, hence perhaps.

clue.text: They drink sap somehow concealed within

indicators.note: within puts the concealed piece inside the rearranged letters
somehow suggests the letters arrive in some other order

explanation.surface: Insects secretly suck plant juices from inside stems.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenfly and blackfly feed by drinking plant sap, so they drink.

clue.text: One who reveres cows (or deer) above crossword solvers, say

indicators.note: above in a down clue puts the deer on top of the next piece

parts.note: a hind is a female deer
solvers are addressed as you, written U in text speak

explanation.surface: A believer in sacred cattle, or deer, stands above the puzzlers.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of Hinduism hold the cow sacred and so revere cows.

clue.text: Readers put off by coy title for obituaries

indicators.note: off suggests the letters are disturbed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Readers are discouraged by a coy heading on a death notices page.
explanation.definitionFit: Departures is a euphemistic heading, as people departing this life are the dead.

clue.text: Sign of approval after denial of shelter

indicators.note: after places the sign of approval behind the denial

explanation.surface: A gesture of agreement follows a refusal to give refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a sheltered corner or recess.

clue.text: Vessels (one going under) returned to embarkation point

indicators.note: returned says the whole sequence is read backwards

parts.note: a sub, a submarine, goes under the water

explanation.surface: Ships, one of them sinking, come back to the port they left from.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus stop is where passengers board, a point of embarkation.

clue.text: "Untouchables" opening with an awkward clunk and then you start — it's like "Friday The Thirteenth"

indicators.note: opening of the film title means its first letter
awkward suggests the letters are clumsily jumbled
start of the word you is its first letter

explanation.surface: A film reviewer's account of a gangster movie's clumsy opening, compared with a horror film.
explanation.definitionFit: Friday the thirteenth is traditionally thought ill-fated.
